speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain feel sharp and localized to the inner side of the knee, and do you notice any swelling or a sensation of the knee giving way? I also need to know if you heard or felt a "pop" at the moment the injury occurred.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain you are describing, located over the medial aspect of the tibia just below the kneecap, sounds like it could be related to your recent increase in volleyball activities. To help narrow this down, can you tell me if the pain is worse when you go up or down stairs, or if you feel any clicking or popping when you bend your knee?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience sharp, localized pain when you press on that specific spot on your shin, and is the pain significantly worse immediately after running or jumping compared to rest? I also need to know if you have noticed any visible swelling or bruising around the knee joint itself.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, recent injuries, swelling or discoloration of the knee, or previous similar complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have no swelling, bruising, or history of trauma, and the pain is localized to the medial tibial tubercle with increased activity, this presentation is highly characteristic of medial tibial stress syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome
